newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: QNI says merger to give chance for growth.
newsitem.headline: QNI says merger to give chance for growth.

text.p: Australian nickel producer QNI Ltd said on Wednesday the merger of its nickel operations with those of South Africa's Gencor Ltd would create a group with the financial strength to take advantage of a range of new growth opportunities.

According to a QNI statement, opportunities included the expansion of Gencor's Cerro Matoso nickel mine in Colombia by the installation of a second furnace line to take production to about 50,000 tonnes per annum of nickel in ferronickel form over the remaining life of the mine.

Other opportunities listed by QNI were the start of nickel mining at Bogota in New Caledonia and the development of an underground mine and concentrator at Maggie Hays/Emily Ann potentially providing feed to a BioNic plant for subsequent refining into marketable nickel and cobalt products.
It said the principal assets of the new company would comprise:
- a 98.9 percent interest in Cerro Matoso, which currently produces 30,000 tonnes of contained nickel in ferronickel form
- the Yabulu nickel refinery in Townsville, Australia, producing some 30,000 tonnes per annum of nickel and 2,000 tonnes per annum of cobalt
- access to nickel in New Caledonia, Indonesia and the Philippines
- a 37.5-percent interest in the Roundtop Joint Venture in Western Australia including the Emily Ann nickel project
- use of Gencor's proprietary nickel processing technologies, BioNIC and GenNIC and those technologies under investigation.
In addition both QNI and Gencor had been pursuing other resource and processing opportunities in New Caledonia, Indonesia, the Caribbean, Canada and Western Australia, it said.

QNI said that because of "de-bottlenecking" and other cost reduction measures being pursued at both principal operations and the company's capacity to initiate new cost competitive products and brownfield expansions, the entity anticipated significant reductions in the cost per lb of nickel produced.
